findings: Two official New York State Senate releases were recovered with nine attributed statement units; the public repository indexes every attributed speaker and links the complete official source.
No Assembly or Senate floor speech on S8319 or A5568A was recovered from the official bill pages, action histories, or bounded newsroom search.

Three local public-event recordings yielded 47 attributed turns for the selected formal-program speakers; the public repository preserves counts and attribution while the transcript derivatives remain protected.

The July 29 authenticated transcript added three selected formal-program speeches: the two state sponsors and Jamie Burkart. The source fingerprint binds the reviewed transcript interface; raw transcript text and authenticated routes remain protected.
openQueries: Continue bounded event-by-event review of Jamie's public recordings and authenticated transcription archive.
Review future committee, floor, press-conference, and rally records as S8319 and A5568A advance.
Classify the remaining full Project X event population without implying support from unreviewed speakers.
Complete a full formal-program attribution ledger for the July 29 report launch without converting shared appearance into endorsement.

boundaries: A press-release quotation is not labeled as a speech or hearing statement.
A bill sponsor memo is not labeled as a speech.
A candidate's later election result does not retroactively change the role held when a speech was delivered.
Authenticated transcript URLs, private file paths, raw audio locators, raw third-party speech, and personal contact details remain outside the public repository.
Protected transcript derivatives preserve speech for authorized research; the public index does not imply that any speaker endorses Jamie or his portfolio.
All means the declared recoverable population, not every supportive statement ever made.
